status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Skills, the check, modifiers, growth model v4 (challenge from the chance on the prompt, the daily total and callings), the recipe-knowledge model (six states), lessons and watching. Every character can learn every skill and every recipe (survival_gdd.md section 7).
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

check_model.effective_skill: S = skill level of action.skill (no specialties in the slice)
check_model.chance: p = clamp(base + (S - D) / slope + sum(modifiers), floor, cap)

outcome_roll.r: uniform 0..1 from the survival RNG stream (saved with the game)
outcome_roll.mishap: failure and r > mishap_r, only on actions that list a hazard

prompt.rule: Show the two or three largest modifiers by size, then one 'what would help' hint chosen from the modifiers the player can change (cover, a flame tinder, mitts, a torch, rest). Materials at risk on failure are listed on a second line.
prompt.example: [E] Make fire · 38% · snow -10%, night -10%, cold hands -10% · Hint: dry birch bark would help
prompt.example_risk: At risk on failure: 1 char cloth, 1 kindling

worked_examples: Backcountry hunter (Survival 32) strikes fire on char cloth (D 20), dry calm day: p = 0.55 + 12/60 = 0.75.
Same hunter on a winter night in falling snow with cold hands: 0.75 - 0.10 - 0.10 = 0.55 (night does not penalise fire-making: the spark is its own light).
Discharged provincial (Survival 25) sets a deadfall (D 25) at dusk with cold hands: 0.55 - 0.10 = 0.45; the prompt shows 'cold hands -10%' and 'Hint: warm your hands at a fire'.
With the hurry toggle every check takes -0.05 and a mishap comes at r > 0.94 instead of 0.97.

modifiers.hint: shield the tinder behind a log or in a shelter

modifiers.light_rule: uses the gameplay light level (seasons.json time_of_day), not the environment rig's sun

modifiers.applies: fine work; Cold stage 'cold' or worse, or no mitts below -10 C
modifiers.hint: warm your hands at a fire

modifiers.applies: fire.strike_flint_steel with birch or cedar bark in the nest
any job run with the hurry toggle (actions.json job_runner.hurry)
a recipe or technique only heard of / only seen (knowledge_model)
modifiers.hint: watch someone do it, or ask to be taught

modifiers.applies: the next attempt of the same action within 120 game minutes of a failure
the taught recipe or technique, for 3 game days

growth_model.gain: k_skill * base_xp * C(p_task) * outcome_mult * L(S) * R(n); plus first_success_bonus * k_skill * base_xp * L(S) once per action per character

challenge.formula: C = clamp((1 - p_task) / ref, min, max) * min(1, p_task / p_low)
challenge.p_task: the chance with only the task's own modifiers (weather, dark, wind, cold hands, damp tinder, the quality standard, second try, untried); impairments (drink, exhaustion, hunger, illness, injury) and hurrying never add challenge

callings.rule: the character's highest working skills at Journeyman or above, ties by id; they use s50_calling

repeat_rule.unit: per action id per game day

daily_cap.counts: every gain in a working skill: checks, first-success bonus, lesson points, pool-doubled practice, watching; points the caps cut from a pool stay in the pool until it expires

growth_model.no_xp_rule: Actions with no cost and no stakes give no experience.
growth_model.weapon_events: weapon skills grow from use only (SurvivalSkills.WEAPON_XP), outside the daily total, never from a crafting roll
growth_model.trade_events: Trade grows from completed trades on one scale, the rv the player gives (barter, sales, labour and a lesson's ask: 1 base xp per 15 d, at most 3 a partner a game day), accounts settled in full (3), promises and labour kept (1), and haggling (a Trade check, base_xp 2), scaled by L(S)
growth_model.backgrounds: no experience multipliers: a background is a head start, never a faster or capped rate

anti_grind.rule: one 600-minute day devoted to one skill: varied work at the edge of ability teaches most, then one action repeated, then easy work (redesign_skills.md 4.8; tested on day plans)

skills.name: Survival
skills.summary: Fire, the brush lean-to, bedding, chinking and banking, foraging and digging roots, plant lore, water, first aid and winter travel. Every camp-craft action rolls against its skill; these roll against Survival.

apprentice.text: Notices ways to carry fire: a live coal in punk or fungus (fire.carry_coal) and lighting tinder with the gunlock (fire.gunlock_ignite). A 6-hour weather outlook in the journal.

journeyman.text: Punk and fungus strike as readily as char cloth (-10 difficulty); lays a long fire down the length of a shelter (fire.lay_long).

adept.text: A partial result can be reworked at half the time instead of starting over.

master.text: Keeps a live coal by habit (carried coals last 1.5x) and a 12-hour outlook.

skills.covers: fire; the brush lean-to, bedding, chinking and banking; foraging, digging roots and plant lore; water; first aid and physick; winter travel and fords

skills.name: Hunting
skills.summary: Tracking, stalking, drives, reading sign, field dressing and skinning (meat yield and pelt grade). Never changes where a shot lands.

apprentice.text: Track age is shown (fresh, hours, a day old).

journeyman.text: Examining an animal within 40 m shows its condition (1-3).

adept.text: Blood trails stay readable twice as long.

master.text: Field dressing yields +10%; an excellent skinning adds a grade.

handling.note: Stealth only: animal detection radius shrinks with skill.

skills.grows_from: tracking, stalking and butchery checks; a clean kill on an unaware animal gives base_xp 3
skills.covers: tracking, stalking, calling, drives, field dressing, skinning, butchery

skills.name: Trapping and Fishing
skills.summary: Stakes and triggers, deadfalls, snares, steel sets and the line; hook and line, nets, weirs, spears and gigs, ice holes; frogs and turtles.

journeyman.text: Walks and resets the line a little faster.

skills.covers: stakes and triggers, deadfalls, snares, steel sets and the line; hook and line, nets, weirs, spears, ice holes; frogs and turtles

skills.name: Provisions
skills.summary: Cooking, jerking, smoking, drying, rendering, salting, parching, sugaring, brewing and storage.

journeyman.text: Food keeps a little longer in your care.

skills.covers: cooking, jerking, smoking, drying, rendering, salting, sugaring, brewing, storage

skills.name: Hide and Needle
skills.summary: Fleshing and stretching, dressing and tanning, rawhide and sinew, cordage, sewing, moccasins, mitts and clothing, mending.

adept.text: A well-handled pelt grades one step better.

skills.covers: fleshing and stretching, dressing and tanning, rawhide and sinew, cordage, sewing, moccasins, mitts and clothing, mending

skills.name: Woodcraft
skills.summary: Felling, splitting and hewing; bark and wood containers; bows, arrows, snowshoes and sleds; the half-faced camp, bark cabins and log cabins; canoe handling.

apprentice.text: Trees fall where you mean them to (no falling-tree mishap below difficulty 30).

journeyman.text: Can lead a cabin raising (neighbours work 20% faster).

adept.text: Snowshoe frames bend true: -10 difficulty on snowshoes.

master.text: Reads water: canoe runs and fords are 10 difficulty easier.

skills.covers: felling, splitting, hewing, bark; carving wood, bone and horn; containers; bows, arrows, snowshoes and sleds; the half-faced camp and cabins; canoes

skills.name: Trade and Diplomacy
skills.summary: Credit, tariffs, gift protocol, interpreting. Languages are separate knowledge entries. Grows from completed trades and honoured agreements, not from clicking haggle or gift.

apprentice.text: The trade window shows each line's cue as a five-step bar.

journeyman.text: Reads a partner's wants and stock without asking; credit lines are 50% larger.

adept.text: Sees the numbers: each line's value to the partner and the floor; argues a tariff 5% down.

master.text: Can hold a trading licence (1765-68) or a merchant's consignment and run a packhorse train.

handling.note: Market spread shrinks linearly with skill (passive haggling).

skills.grows_from: completed trades, sales and barters on one scale (1 base xp per 15 d of the rv the player gives, at most 3 a partner a game day), haggling checks, accounts settled in full, and promises and labour kept, scaled by the level curve L(S)

skills.name: Marksmanship
skills.summary: Musket and pistol handling. Never moves the aim point, never adds aim assist, never changes zeroing.
skills.grows_from: use only: a completed reload 0.02 skill points (0.01 when no threat is near), a hit beyond 30 m 0.05, a clean kill 0.1; the daily cap applies. Casting balls gives no Marksmanship.

handling.note: Linear from level 0 (the current game feel, x1.0) to level 100. Hard cap 15-20%.

skills.name: Archery
skills.summary: Bow handling. Never moves the aim point.
skills.grows_from: use only: a full draw released 0.01, a hit beyond 20 m 0.05, a clean kill 0.1. Making arrows is a Survival craft.

skills.name: Close Combat
skills.summary: Saber, tomahawk and spear, in hand and thrown. Handling only.
skills.grows_from: use only: a landed blow or throw 0.03 (sparring at the fort counts at half).

handling_cap.rule: Skill never aims for the player: no aim assist, no aim-point change, no zeroing change. Level 0 equals the current game feel; skills only improve handling toward the cap. Background perks never add to handling (review 2, issue 6).

aliases.growth_model.tier_mult: retired in v4 (the level curve L(S))
aliases.growth_model.typical_day: retired in v4 (the anti-grind day plans and the harness pacing gates)
aliases.backgrounds.xp_mult: retired in v4: no background experience multipliers
aliases.tier_unlocks.unlocks: now notices: reaching a tier makes the techniques heard of; nothing is locked

skill_of_prefix.rule: Every action id, live and backlog, maps to a skill; the first matching prefix wins (redesign_skills.md 3.3). The working roster is the default pending the user's choice (GDD section 19, question 1); the named alternative is one skill, Handicraft, with trapping, fishing and provisions staying in Survival.

knowledge_model.gated: recipes (rcp.*), techniques (know.*) and actions with technique: true; never the plain verbs
knowledge_model.id_rule: Knowledge is kept on the technique id where one covers the recipe (a recipe's knowledge field); otherwise on the recipe or action id

unknown.except: a notice (recipes.json routes.trial.notice) moves it to heard_of

promote.to_known: a success or partial from heard_of or seen; clues_needed clues; a lesson; the background; common knowledge

watch.time: the watcher is charged the watched job's game minutes on their own clock

knowledge_model.tier_notices: reaching a tier moves the skill's tier_unlocks notices from unknown to heard_of (a journal line)
knowledge_model.routes_rule: every recipe and technique lists at least two routes to known, at least one needing no coin and no particular background (rule L2); community-held knowledge lists taught and watched only (redesign_skills.md 5.4)
knowledge_model.community_held: learned only by being taught by that community, by its choice, after consultation; no trial route
knowledge_model.recipe_book: a journal page: each entry's state, successes, clues, teachers known, where it was seen, and the origin note

trap.snare_set.text: A noose of cordage on a bent sapling across a run would hold a hare.

preserve.cache_pit.text: Meat hung high on a pole between two trees would keep from the wolves.

knowledge_model.notices_rule: Only simple, generic work has notices (redesign_skills.md 8); complex work (snowshoes, dressing a hide, moccasins, the half-faced camp, ice fishing) needs heard of first, from examining the thing, talk, a lesson or watching.

knowledge.name: Making ashiko (foot claws) from the woods
knowledge.gates: the knapping stone's ashiko copies (CampStation STONE climbing_claws_wood, _bone, _stone: needs_know; heard of lets a make be tried, and a make promotes it)
knowledge.origin: Handed-down knowledge (user 2026-09-29: 'iron is the real one the others will be handed down knowledge'): the old hunter's copies of the Japanese ashiko, from a Dutch sailor's iron pair (Dejima, the Dutch post in Japan, 1641-1854). The tale is the game's own.

knowledge.name: Dressing deerskins
knowledge.notes: Skilled, heavy work that made skins marketable (E:3.1). The backlog's settler farmer no longer teaches it: Palatine households tanned with bark or tawed (know.bark_tanning, M5).
knowledge.origin: A Native method of dressing skins (brains, working and smoke), widely learned by colonial hunters; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).

knowledge.name: Making snowshoes
knowledge.origin: A Native form, learned by colonial hunters and soldiers; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).
knowledge.later_teachers: archetype:canadien_voyageur, archetype:town_hunter (M4-M5, after sign-off for the town hunter)

knowledge.name: Laying a canoe bed
knowledge.origin: A Native craft (the Algonquian nations' bark canoe), adopted by French voyageurs and colonial traders; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).
knowledge.notes: The building bed: stakes driven into gravel by the water to hold the mould the bark is shaped on (the frame, the length and the sheer set by eye and measure).

knowledge.name: Fitting and sewing bark
knowledge.origin: A Native craft (the Algonquian nations' bark canoe), adopted by French voyageurs and colonial traders; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).
knowledge.notes: Laying the bark skin over the bed with even pressure, gores set in for the sides, and stitching it with spruce root through awl holes.

knowledge.name: Gunwales, ribs and sheathing
knowledge.origin: A Native craft (the Algonquian nations' bark canoe), adopted by French voyageurs and colonial traders; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).
knowledge.notes: Sandwiching the bark between inner and outer gunwales, pegged; then steamed cedar ribs and sheathing driven tight to stretch the skin.

knowledge.name: Pitching seams
knowledge.origin: A Native craft (the Algonquian nations' bark canoe), adopted by French voyageurs and colonial traders; wording under consultation (GDD section 13, rule 9).
knowledge.notes: Sealing every seam with rendered spruce pitch, tallow and charcoal, spread evenly, no thin place.
